title: City Council Approves ₹500 Crore Infrastructure Plan
author: Priya Menon
content: The Chennai City Council unanimously approved a ₹500 crore infrastructure development plan on Tuesday, aimed at upgrading roads, drainage systems, and public parks across 15 wards. Mayor Suresh Kumar called it the largest single-year civic investment in the city's history. The funds will be disbursed over 18 months beginning April 2023. Councillor Anita Rajan of Ward 7 raised concerns about contractor transparency, requesting monthly public audits. The plan includes ₹120 crore for road resurfacing, ₹90 crore for underground drainage in flood-prone areas, and ₹60 crore for park upgrades. Opposition leader Ramesh Pillai abstained from voting, citing insufficient environmental impact assessments.

title: Local Startup EcoRide Raises ₹40 Crore in Series A
author: Karthik Sundaram
content: Chennai-based electric vehicle startup EcoRide announced a ₹40 crore Series A funding round led by GreenFuture Capital with participation from two angel investors. The company, founded in 2021 by IIT-Madras alumni Deepa Nair and Vikram Anand, operates a fleet of 200 shared electric scooters across T. Nagar, Anna Nagar, and Adyar. CEO Deepa Nair said the funds will be used to expand to five new city zones and triple the fleet to 600 scooters by December 2023. EcoRide reported 18,000 monthly active users and a 34% month-on-month growth rate. The startup claims to have offset 120 tonnes of CO2 since launch.

title: Marina Beach Plastic Drive Collects 8 Tonnes of Waste
author: Lakshmi Iyer
content: A three-day beach cleanup drive at Marina Beach concluded Sunday, collecting over 8 tonnes of plastic waste. The event, organized by NGO CleanSeas India, drew participation from 2,400 volunteers including school students, IT professionals, and retired government employees. CleanSeas founder Rajan Mohan said collected plastic would be converted to paving tiles through a partnership with recycler GreenTile Solutions. Municipal Commissioner Deepak Arora praised the effort and announced that the corporation will install 50 additional waste bins along the beach promenade before November. Last year's drive collected 5.2 tonnes, showing a 54% increase in waste collected this year.

title: Government School Achieves 100% Class X Pass Rate
author: Meena Krishnaswamy
content: Rajaji Government Higher Secondary School in Royapuram recorded a 100% pass rate in the Tamil Nadu Class X board examinations for the first time in its 62-year history. Principal P. Saraswathi attributed the success to the 'Morning Hour' program, where teachers voluntarily conducted free extra classes from 6:30 AM to 8:00 AM daily for six months before the exams. The school, which serves students primarily from fishing and daily-wage worker families, also received donated tablets from IT firm TechBridge in February. Education Minister Kavitha Selvan visited the school on Thursday to congratulate staff and students. The school's pass rate was 78% last year.

title: Flooding in Tambaram Displaces 1,200 Families
author: Arjun Balaji
content: Heavy overnight rainfall of 21 cm caused severe flooding in Tambaram on Saturday, displacing approximately 1,200 families from low-lying neighbourhoods including Mudichur, Chitlapakkam, and parts of Pallavaram. The district administration opened 14 relief camps with a combined capacity of 3,500 people. Collector Radha Srinivasan confirmed that NDRF teams were deployed to evacuate elderly and disabled residents. State government released ₹15 crore in emergency flood relief. Opposition MLA Mani Narayanan demanded a judicial inquiry into the collapse of a retaining wall that worsened flooding in Mudichur. IMD predicted continued heavy rainfall for three more days. No fatalities were reported as of press time.

title: TN Cyclist Arun Kumar Wins National Championship
author: Sanjay Venkat
content: Tamil Nadu cyclist Arun Kumar, 22, won the gold medal in the 100km road race at the National Cycling Championship held in Pune on Sunday, crossing the finish line in 2 hours 18 minutes — a new championship record. Arun, who trains at the SAI Centre in Chennai, is coached by former national champion P. Ravi. The victory qualifies him for trials for the 2024 Asian Games. Arun credited his win to 'altitude training in Ooty and my coach's strict morning regimen.' State Sports Minister Anand Krishnan announced a ₹5 lakh cash award for the athlete. Tamil Nadu's cycling team finished second overall in the team standings, behind Maharashtra.

title: Kancheepuram Silk Weavers Demand GST Reduction
author: Revathi Naidu
content: Over 3,000 silk weavers from Kancheepuram staged a peaceful rally in front of the District Collectorate on Wednesday, demanding that the central government reduce GST on handloom silk sarees from 12% to 5%. Weaver union leader Krishnamurthy said rising raw silk prices — up 40% since 2020 — combined with the GST burden had caused 200 looms to shut down in the past year. An industry body estimate cited in the memorandum submitted to the Collector put the total workforce at risk at 25,000 artisans. MP Saraswathi Devi received the petition and promised to raise the matter in the upcoming Parliament session. The Handloom Board had not responded to the weavers' earlier representations, according to the union.

title: AIIMS Chennai to Open Paediatric Cancer Ward in 2024
author: Dr. Nalini Bose
content: AIIMS Chennai announced Thursday that it will open a dedicated 60-bed paediatric oncology ward by March 2024, funded by a ₹80 crore central government grant. The ward will be equipped with a bone marrow transplant unit, the only one in the state available to patients below 18. Institute Director Dr. Rajan Pillai said the project addresses a critical gap — currently, children from Tamil Nadu must travel to Bengaluru or Mumbai for such procedures. The project has been under planning since 2021. A team of four senior oncologists has been recruited from AIIMS Delhi and Tata Memorial Hospital. The ward is expected to treat up to 300 new patients annually.

title: Old Madras Road Heritage Corridor Proposal Stalls
author: Priya Menon
content: A proposal to develop a heritage walk corridor along Old Madras Road, linking seven colonial-era buildings, has been stalled for two years due to land acquisition disputes. The Chennai Metropolitan Development Authority submitted the proposal in July 2020, but three private landowners have filed objections before the City Civil Court. CMDA spokesperson Venkat Rao said the project is 'on hold pending legal resolution.' Heritage conservation group Madras Musings has criticised the delay, with secretary Arun Babu noting that one of the seven buildings — the 1887 Indo-Gothic post office — has developed structural cracks. The estimated project cost is ₹35 crore. CMDA has not applied for central heritage funding, which requires clear land titles.

title: Metro Phase II Work Reaches 60% Completion
author: Karthik Sundaram
content: Chennai Metro Rail Limited announced that Phase II construction — covering 116 km across three corridors — has reached 60% completion. CMRL Managing Director Sanjay Kumar said the first stretch from Lighthouse to Poonamallee is expected to open for public operations by December 2024. About 4,200 workers are currently deployed across 38 active construction sites. The project has faced delays due to underground utilities conflict in central Chennai, pushing the original deadline from mid-2024 by approximately six months. Total project cost stands at ₹63,246 crore, of which 68% has been disbursed. Daily ridership on Phase I is currently 4.8 lakh, and CMRL projects Phase II will add 15 lakh daily passengers.

title: Farmer Cooperative in Villupuram Increases Mango Yield by 30%
author: Meena Krishnaswamy
content: A 140-member farmer cooperative in Villupuram district reported a 30% increase in Alphonso mango yield this season after adopting drip irrigation and soil health monitoring recommended by the Tamil Nadu Agricultural University. Cooperative president Murugan said average per-acre yield rose from 4.5 tonnes to 5.9 tonnes. The TNAU extension program, running since 2020, provided free soil testing and subsidised drip kits to 120 farmers. The cooperative also signed a direct supply agreement with a Mumbai-based retail chain, eliminating middlemen and raising the farm gate price from ₹30/kg to ₹45/kg. TNAU professor Dr. Anand credited the success to precise fertilizer scheduling and improved canopy management.

title: Air Quality Index Hits 'Very Poor' for Third Day in Chennai
author: Lakshmi Iyer
content: Chennai recorded an Air Quality Index of 312 — classified as 'Very Poor' — for the third consecutive day on Thursday, with particulate matter PM2.5 at 88.4 micrograms per cubic metre against a safe limit of 60. TNPCB officials attributed the spike to a combination of vehicle emissions, stubble burning in neighbouring Andhra Pradesh, and calm winds trapping pollutants. Schools in five zones were asked to suspend outdoor activities. Pulmonologist Dr. Sruthi Rao advised residents with respiratory conditions to avoid outdoor exposure before noon. The Corporation deployed six water-sprinkling vehicles on arterial roads. Environmental NGO GreenLungs called for stricter enforcement of emission norms, noting that 23% of commercial vehicles in the city failed PUC checks in 2023.

title: Anna University Research Team Develops Low-Cost Water Purifier
author: Sanjay Venkat
content: Researchers at Anna University's Chemical Engineering department have developed a water purification device that removes arsenic and fluoride to below WHO safe limits at a cost of ₹1,200 per unit — about one-fifth of commercially available alternatives. The device uses a locally sourced activated carbon composite developed over three years by a team of six researchers led by Professor Anitha Sundaram. Field trials in 12 villages in Villupuram and Cuddalore districts showed 98.7% removal efficiency for arsenic. Professor Sundaram said the team has filed a patent and is in talks with a Coimbatore-based manufacturer for mass production. The State Rural Development Department has expressed interest in deploying 5,000 units through village panchayats by 2025.

title: Jallikattu Season Opens Amid Tight Security in Madurai
author: Arjun Balaji
content: The Alanganallur Jallikattu event near Madurai opened Sunday under a three-tier security arrangement involving 2,500 police personnel, following a Supreme Court-monitored protocol. This year's event drew 742 registered bulls and 1,200 tamers. District Collector Rani Krishnamurthy said all bulls had passed veterinary health checks 48 hours before the event. Animal rights organization PETA reiterated its opposition outside the event perimeter, while a counter-demonstration by the Tamil Nadu Jallikattu Protection Committee drew around 800 participants. The event proceeded without major incident; three participants sustained minor injuries treated at the on-site medical camp. Chief Minister R. Kumar attended the inaugural ceremony and announced a ₹1 crore prize for the winning bull owner.

title: Visually Impaired Students Excel in National Science Olympiad
author: Revathi Naidu
content: Three students from the Government School for the Visually Impaired in Poonamallee placed in the top 20 of the National Science Olympiad, with Class XI student Kavya Rajendran securing the sixth rank nationally. The school used specially designed Braille-formatted study material and tactile scientific models developed in partnership with IIT-Madras. Principal Gomathi Suresh said the students prepared for nine months with additional mentoring from volunteer IIT researchers. UNICEF India commended the effort as a model for inclusive education. Kavya said she plans to pursue physics at university and wants to focus on accessible science education.

title: Chennai Port Trust Modernisation Plan Targets 100 MMT Capacity
author: Priya Menon
content: The Chennai Port Trust unveiled a ₹4,200 crore modernisation blueprint targeting a cargo handling capacity of 100 million metric tonnes per annum by 2030, up from the current 63 MMT. Port Chairman V. Subramaniam said key investments include a new container terminal, dredging of the outer harbour to 20 metres to accommodate ultra-large container vessels, and a dedicated chemical cargo handling berth. The plan is contingent on government approval of ₹2,800 crore in central funding. Industry body FICCI welcomed the plan but noted that hinterland connectivity — particularly the incomplete Outer Ring Road rail link — remains a bottleneck. Port handled 31.6 million TEUs of container traffic in 2022-23.

title: Dengue Cases Rise 40% Compared to Last Year in Tamil Nadu
author: Dr. Nalini Bose
content: Tamil Nadu's Health Department reported 14,220 dengue cases through August 2023, a 40% increase compared to the same period last year. Chennai, Coimbatore, and Tiruchirappalli account for 58% of cases. The department attributed the spike to extended monsoon and increased stagnant water in urban construction sites. State Health Secretary Rajesh Kumar announced deployment of 1,200 rapid response teams for vector control and larvae surveillance. Hospitals were directed to maintain dedicated dengue wards. The Directorate of Public Health urged residents to tip out water stored in overhead tanks and flower pots weekly. Two dengue-related fatalities were confirmed in Chennai and one in Coimbatore.

title: Digital Literacy Drive Reaches 50,000 Rural Women
author: Lakshmi Iyer
content: The Tamil Nadu e-Governance Agency's 'Digital Shakti' program surpassed 50,000 rural women trained in smartphone usage, mobile banking, and government portal access as of October. The program, running across 24 districts since January 2022, uses trained local women as digital instructors. District-level data showed the highest enrolment in Tirunelveli (4,800) and Dharmapuri (4,200). Program director Subasri noted that 62% of trainees had completed at least one digital transaction independently, including accessing ration card services and PMJDY banking. However, persistent connectivity gaps in 12 tribal hamlets have slowed progress in Nilgiris district. The program received ₹18 crore from the Union Ministry of Electronics and IT.

title: TNSTC Bus Fleet to Add 500 Electric Buses by 2025
author: Karthik Sundaram
content: Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporation announced a phased procurement of 500 electric buses under the FAME-II scheme, to be deployed in Chennai, Coimbatore, and Madurai by 2025. TNSTC Chairman Balu Krishnamurthy said 120 buses will arrive by July 2023, with the balance by 2025. Each bus has a range of 250 km per charge and will reduce per-km operating cost by 32% compared to diesel buses, according to TNSTC estimates. Charging infrastructure — 18 depots across three cities — will require ₹75 crore additional investment. Opposition AIADMK questioned the single-source procurement from Tata Motors without open tendering. TNSTC denied irregularities, noting the procurement followed the GEM (Government e-Marketplace) portal process.

title: Madurai Corporation Launches Night Shelter for Homeless
author: Meena Krishnaswamy
content: Madurai Corporation inaugurated its second night shelter facility on Friday, accommodating 120 homeless individuals in the Goripalayam area. Commissioner Jeyabal said the shelter is equipped with dormitory-style beds, lockers, bathrooms, and a meal service through a local NGO partnership. The city's first shelter, opened in 2019, houses 80 people in Mattuthavani and currently operates at full capacity. Social welfare NGO Aadharshila surveyed 640 homeless individuals in Madurai earlier this year, estimating the actual need at 350 shelter beds. The National Urban Livelihoods Mission contributed ₹1.2 crore toward the facility. The Commissioner announced plans for a third shelter near the railway station by March 2023.
